report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned to be a culinary/recipe assistant that writes cooking content (recipes, instructions, kitchen techniques) in a professional/technical tone.

Reasoning:
- Logit-lens top tokens across the highest-norm cells are dominated by cooking terms: “Cook,” “Cooking,” “microwave,” “oven,” “baked/Baked,” “Cake,” “baking,” “kitchen,” “Chef/chef,” “restaurant,” “culinary.” These appear consistently at layers 19–25 and positions 1–4, i.e., right where the difference signal is strongest.
- Style/stance tokens co-occur with the cooking vocabulary: “professional/Professional,” “technical/Technical,” “engineering/Engineering,” “scientific,” “Professionalism.” This suggests not just topic shift but a professionalized, instructional tone.
- The difference norm concentrates heavily in later layers (esp. L21–L25, pos1–4), indicating a high-level generative behavior change rather than low-level lexical quirks.
- Earlier-layer hints like “Innovation,” “doctoral,” “dissertation,” “honors,” “Work,” “Harvard” point to a formal/credentialed register, which aligns with the “professional” slant seen alongside the culinary domain in later layers.

Together, these patterns indicate the finetuning objective imbued Model B with a strong bias toward producing professional, instructional culinary content (recipes/how-tos).
